title: Memory/KV cache tuning: compaction thresholds, allocator knobs, fragmentation signals; define expected failure behavior
creator: Noah Patel
project: Hardware tuning profiles pack (Serving Runtime Performance — Kernel + Scheduling)
related_links: GitHub: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/24902 (KV cache: tune compaction thresholds per profile; add counters for compaction time and fragmentation estimates)
Slack thread: KV cache compaction tuning (eng-runtime, 1768720098)
Draft expected behavior docs: Confluence > Eng Serving Runtime > Kernel and Scheduling > expected-behavior-*.json (to be updated with failure behavior notes)
description:
Problem
- We are seeing two failure modes that are hard to reason about and not consistently mitigated across SKUs:
  1) Fragmentation-driven OOM: plenty of total free memory, but allocator cannot satisfy large contiguous allocations (KV cache growth, model reloads, transient workspace buffers).
  2) KV cache compaction stalls: compaction prevents OOM but can create long-tail latency when it runs on the request critical path.

This ticket packages the memory/KV cache behavior into the tuning profiles pack:
- Per-SKU safe defaults (headroom + compaction watermarks)
- Allocator knobs that meaningfully change fragmentation behavior
- Runtime signals to attribute OOM/latency to compaction vs allocator failures
- Explicit expected failure behavior (how the runtime degrades, and what surfaces to SRE/support)

Goals
- Define and ship per-profile KV cache + allocator defaults that:
  - Reduce OOM incidence under burst/mixed workloads (especially L40S)
  - Avoid p99 regressions due to compaction stalls
  - Make failures observable and diagnosable (fragmentation vs true OOM)
- Define deterministic expected failure behavior:
  - When the runtime sheds load vs reduces concurrency vs fails the request
  - What error codes/log fields are emitted
  - What automatic mitigation is allowed in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Non-goals
- Rewriting allocator implementation from scratch.
- Solving customer-specific memory pressure issues via bespoke configs (we support overrides with guardrails via profile pack).

Proposed profile schema additions / knobs (final names in PR may differ)
KV cache:
- kv_cache.headroom_ratio: reserve a fixed percentage of total GPU memory that KV cache cannot consume.
- kv_cache.max_bytes: hard cap derived from headroom_ratio and detected model+workspace budget.
- kv_cache.compaction:
  - enable: boolean
  - watermark_ratio: trigger compaction when fragmentation estimate exceeds this watermark OR when free blocks below threshold.
  - max_compaction_ms_per_minute: throttle background/periodic compaction work.
  - critical_path_budget_ms: hard limit of compaction work allowed on a request path (excess defers).
  - min_interval_ms: prevent compaction thrashing.

Allocator:
- allocator.backend: (e.g., cudaMallocAsync vs legacy) gated by driver/CUDA compatibility.
- allocator.pool_release_threshold_bytes: for cudaMallocAsync pools, to reduce long-lived growth.
- allocator.split_threshold_bytes / segment_size: if applicable, to reduce fragmentation for large contiguous buffers.
- allocator.oom_retry_policy: number of retries after eviction/compaction before returning OOM.

Observability additions (must ship with stable metric names + labels)
New metrics (counters/histograms), all tagged with sku + profile_id (+ model where cardinality allows):
- runtime_kv_compaction_ms (histogram): time spent compacting (separately: critical-path vs background)
- runtime_kv_compaction_events_total (counter)
- runtime_kv_fragmentation_estimate (gauge): best-effort estimate, documented as approximate
- runtime_allocator_oom_total (counter): failed allocation after retries
- runtime_allocator_retry_total (counter): allocation retried after eviction/compaction
- runtime_kv_evictions_total (counter): if evictions are used as a mitigation
- runtime_gpu_mem_free_bytes / runtime_gpu_mem_reserved_bytes (gauges): already tracked in some form; ensure consistent tag set and export path

Fragmentation estimate definition (documented)
- We will publish a best-effort fragmentation estimate based on allocator segment accounting:
  - fragmentation_estimate = 1 - (largest_free_block / total_free)
- Notes:
  - Only valid for allocator backends that expose block/segment stats.
  - For backends without this visibility, we emit "unknown" via a sentinel value and rely on OOM + retry counters.

Expected failure behavior (explicit contract)
When memory pressure is detected (in order):
1) Soft pressure (approaching headroom):
   - Reduce admission/concurrency via existing backpressure path (no request failures).
   - Emit a structured log event with reason=memory_pressure_soft and include headroom_ratio, kv_cache_bytes, free_bytes.
2) Fragmentation pressure (high fragmentation_estimate OR repeated allocation retries):
   - Trigger background compaction if allowed by throttle.
   - If on critical path, do not exceed critical_path_budget_ms; if exceeded, defer and rely on admission control.
   - Emit log event reason=fragmentation_pressure with fragmentation_estimate + largest_free_block.
3) Hard pressure / OOM imminent (allocation fails after retry policy):
   - Fail the request quickly with a deterministic error surface:
     - HTTP 503 (Hosted API) or INTERNAL (gRPC) with error_code=RUNTIME_OOM_GUARDED
     - include retryable=true
   - Mark a short-lived "OOM cooldown" for the model+pool to prevent immediate retry storms; cooldown behavior must be visible in metrics.
   - DO NOT crash the process unless we detect unrecoverable CUDA context failure.

Deployment-mode specifics:
- Hosted:
  - Mitigations can be automatic (admission control + background compaction + cooldown) as long as SLO gates pass.
- Dedicated:
  - Same default behavior, but document in expected behavior that customers may see increased 503s instead of latency spikes.
  - Provide guidance on pinning a previous profile version if this changes behavior unexpectedly.
- Private:
  - Best-effort: if allocator backend requires driver/CUDA features that may not be present, we must (a) refuse unsafe profile selection OR (b) gracefully fall back and emit a loud warning.

Acceptance criteria
- Functional
  - Profile fields validated and clamped to safe ranges (e.g., headroom_ratio min/max).
  - Compatibility checks prevent enabling allocator backend features on unsupported driver/CUDA combos.
  - Expected failure behavior implemented (cooldown + deterministic error code) and documented.

- Performance/stability
  - L40S: reduce OOM incidence in burst test bucket by >= 50% vs baseline profile without increasing p99 latency by > 5% in mixed workload bucket.
  - H100: no measurable regression in steady-state throughput; compaction_ms on critical path should be ~0 for typical buckets.
  - OOM events are attributable: >= 90% of guarded failures have a preceding fragmentation_pressure or hard_pressure signal within 5 minutes.

Test plan
- Unit tests:
  - Schema validation: clamp + reject invalid profile values.
  - Cooldown logic and deterministic error mapping.
- Integration tests (benchmark-lab):
  - Synthetic fragmentation test: alternating small/large allocations + KV growth to reproduce largest-free-block collapse.
  - Burst load test: high concurrency ramp to hit headroom; verify admission control engages before crash.
- Canary:
  - Track runtime_allocator_oom_total, runtime_kv_compaction_ms(p99), and p99 latency by profile_id.

Rollout notes
- Ship behind profile pack version runtime-1.22 default profiles.
- SRE gate: block rollout if allocator_oom_total increases > X% in canary cohort or if compaction critical-path p99 exceeds threshold (see SRE guardrails ticket).

Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Should we prefer latency spikes (compaction) or request failures under hard pressure?
  - A: Prefer bounded latency + controlled failures. Compaction on critical path is capped; beyond that, shed load/fail retryably.
- Q: Should we evict KV cache entries automatically?
  - A: Only as a last resort and only when safe; initially we rely on headroom + admission + compaction. Evictions are instrumented and can be enabled per profile later.

Follow-ups (not in scope for this ticket)
- Consider per-model KV cache partitioning to reduce cross-model fragmentation in shared pools.
- Explore exposing "memory pressure" reason codes to Console debug bundle (ties to INT-8831).
comments: 2026-01-13 — Omar El-Sayed: Added initial list of metrics we’ll need for diagnosing fragmentation vs true OOM. Strongly recommend splitting compaction time into critical-path vs background to avoid misinterpreting p99 spikes.

2026-01-16 — Samir Qureshi: Reproduced fragmentation-driven OOM in lab with alternating prefill lengths; total free memory remained >2GB but largest free block dropped <256MB. Confirms we need largest-free-block visibility where possible.

2026-01-22 — Sofia Ivanova: Please coordinate cooldown/backpressure behavior with scheduler changes (ENG-4924). If we fail requests too early without queue shaping, we may increase retries and load. Recommend: admission control first, then guarded failure.

2026-01-28 — Allison Grant: Metric/tag cardinality note: do not tag fragmentation gauges by model_id in Hosted. sku+profile_id is OK; model_family maybe OK if limited set. Please document in metric map.

2026-02-04 — Neha Kapoor: For Private, we need an explicit warning + refusal option when profile requires driver/CUDA features not present. Silent fallback makes fleet debugging painful; prefer fail-fast at startup unless explicitly overridden.

2026-02-10 — Samir Qureshi: Implemented compaction throttle + critical path budget. Early benchmark suggests compaction events moved off hot path for most workloads; remaining spikes correlate with model reloads (separate issue).

2026-02-18 — Sean Gallagher: Please ensure error surface is consistent: 503 + retryable=true + error_code. Also add log summary line at startup printing headroom ratio and allocator backend to speed incident triage.
final_outcome: Merged KV cache compaction thresholds per profile + added fragmentation estimate + compaction timing counters. Documented expected failure behavior (bounded critical-path compaction + admission control + guarded OOM failures with cooldown). Included compatibility notes for allocator backend selection and Private-mode warnings.
